diagram.manim_description: Draw a square 8 by 8 chess board, centred on a plain white (BG) 16:9 canvas; the board height is 88% of the canvas height and the board width equals its height. All 64 squares are equal squares. Number the rows 1 to 8 from top to bottom and the columns 1 to 8 from left to right (these numbers are only used here, they are not drawn). The top-left square (row 1, column 1) is a dark square. A square is dark when row + column is even and light when row + column is odd. Fill dark squares GUIDE (#6B7280) and light squares BG (white). Give every square a 2 px INK outline and the whole board a 3 px INK outline. Place exactly 8 knights, one on each of these 8 light squares: row 1 columns 2, 4, 6 and 8; row 2 columns 1, 3, 5 and 7. Draw each knight as the chess-knight glyph ♞ (U+265E) in ANSWER green (#009E73), centred in its square, glyph height 70% of the square height. Rows 3 to 8 hold no pieces and the dark squares hold no pieces. Draw no letters, numbers, arrows, labels or any other text anywhere.
must_not_show: row numbers, column numbers or file letters a to h
knight-move arrows or the small 5 by 5 demonstration board of the book
a 10 by 10 board (the book prints 10 x 10, this figure is the standard 8 x 8 chess board)
any knight on a dark square or in rows 3 to 8
the owl, the children or any other illustration of the book page
accuracy_checks: board is 8 rows by 8 columns: 64 squares, 32 dark and 32 light, top-left square dark
exactly 8 knights: 4 in row 1 (columns 2, 4, 6, 8) and 4 in row 2 (columns 1, 3, 5, 7)
every knight square has row + column odd, so every knight is on a light square
for all 28 pairs of knights the absolute row difference and column difference are never (1, 2) or (2, 1), so no knight attacks another
the 8 knights occupy exactly the 8 light squares of the first two rows (4 + 4)
